The skin shows local vibration. Your ears hear the sum. Opposite motion can cancel.

a small field guide

Follow what remains.

Three pockets share a living vibration. A sound can become quiet without being gone.

01

Wake the skin

Tap any pocket. Rub it to feed the motion. Rest a finger or hold the mouse still to absorb it.

02

Catch the movement

Drag either narrow waist. Up opens it; down closes it. On a vertical pod, drag right to open and left to close.

03

Find the quiet

Open both waists fully. Tap one end, then rest on the middle for two seconds. Lift your hand. If the ends still move, change a waist and listen.

A little further

Close one waist and rub an end strongly. Its vibration can become reluctant to leave even when you reopen the waist. A gentle touch can help it travel.

For a quiet transfer: close the waist nearest one end and open the far waist. Tap that end gently. Over several seconds, open the near waist, then close the far one.

What is happening?

Three coupled nonlinear resonators retain their amplitude and phase. Moving contact feeds vibration, still contact damps it, and stronger vibration rings slightly higher. Open waists exchange the actual oscillation. Nothing schedules a hush or a release.

The sound is a fixed mono pickup with gentle saturation after summing. The soft body is a drawing, not a fluid simulation; its ridges show vibration slowed down so you can see the phase. All sound is made here in your browser.

Keyboard & running locally

1 2 3 tap the pockets. Hold Shift with a number to damp. Tab to a waist and use arrow keys; Home closes it and End opens it. M mutes, R resets, D inspects.

Get the Periodic Tables source, then run python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory dist and open http://localhost:8000/instruments/hushpod/. No installation or build step.

Origins, source & limits

Hushpod is an independent instrument from James Stewart’s collaborative instrument study, built with ChatGPT / Codex. This edition reuses the October 16, 2026 prototype’s simulation and sound processor unchanged, with navigation, accessibility, and audio-lifecycle improvements.

The model measures oscillator action, not mechanical energy in joules. The skin is an illustration of the model. With reduced motion enabled, brightness still follows stored vibration while the rippling displacement stops. This is an exploratory prototype, not a validated physical device.

Source & integration notes · MIT license · Provenance. No imported recordings, fonts, or artwork; sound is synthesized in your browser. The wider study record is still being preserved.
